title: Purification of viruses via CsCl gradient and ultracentrifugation
author: Jozef Nissimov
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.d9k94v
materials: Purification of viruses via CsCl gradient and ultracentrifugation
Dispense above into four 15 mL falcon tubes.

steps.title: Add sample and dissolve CsCl
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL of the virus‑containing sample into each Beckman ultracentrifuge tube and shake the tube until the cesium chloride (CsCl) is completely dissolved.

steps.title: Layer CsCl gradient
steps.instruction: Starting with the densest solution, carefully layer the CsCl gradient blocks into the tube, adding 3 mL per layer. Use a pipette or pour slowly (like Irish coffee) and take extra time to ensure smooth, distinct layers.

steps.title: Run ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Place the tube in the rotor and centrifuge at 25 000 rpm for 3 h at 15 °C, using a maximum acceleration and deceleration setting of 9.

steps.title: Retrieve ultracentrifuge tube
steps.instruction: After the run, open the centrifuge chambers carefully and pull out the ultracentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Clamp tube in holder
steps.instruction: Clamp the ultracentrifuge tube with a multipurpose extension tube clamp holder (as shown in Figure 1A).

steps.title: Prepare needle‑syringe
steps.instruction: Assemble a sterile needle and syringe, ensuring that no air bubbles remain in the syringe.

steps.title: Puncture and extract band
steps.instruction: Gently puncture a hole in the ultracentrifuge tube exactly at the location where the visible band appears. Extract the band gently with the syringe (Figure 2B). If multiple bands are present, start with the uppermost band and work downward.

steps.title: Weigh extracted material
steps.instruction: Pre‑weigh a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube before adding the extracted band volume. After transfer, re‑weigh the tube containing the band extract and record the weight difference.

steps.title: Calculate buoyant density
steps.instruction: Calculate the buoyant density of the recovered material using the measured weight difference and the known volume of the extracted band.
